name: btor2-bmc
notes: Bounded model checking for BTOR2 (bit-vectors, signed division, arrays by the eager reduction with Ackermann congruence and extensionality lemmas; nested arrays refused with a partial): the program is bit-blasted per frame to a hash-consed AIG, Tseitin-encoded, and decided by a generated CDCL SAT solver; a sat model is replayed through the interpreter semantics before it is emitted, so a too-sparse instantiation can only cost a witness, never invent one; an unsat at every depth <= k is a bare universal claim all(k) — no certificate schema yet, so it floors at claimed. The conflict budget and structural caps derive from the wall argument, never the clock: 400 conflicts/s, clauses 30000/s ceilinged at 18M, AIG nodes 20000/s in [4M, 12M]. The accelerator solve_fast.c mirrors the reference formula by formula and is admitted by byte-agreement on the corpus (rebuild: cc -O2 -o solve_fast solve_fast.c). ledger.py reports cleared bits per universal claim.
